$comment: See host.schema.json's own $comment for why every field lives inside the `script:` object, name included. No vars (scripts don't have them) and no extends (the Extends section explicitly lists environment/network/host/container only, not script). people IS included despite the Script section's prose field-list omitting it, because the canonical vuln-sqli.yaml example uses it and 'Referencing a person' says people works on any object -- flagged back to the team as a doc inconsistency worth a one-line fix.

script.description: A script: a template rendered per host per team before it runs, with the environment's vars, people data, and host/network facts all in scope. Its source file (.sh/.ps1/.bat) sits beside this definition. Its own tags, findings, and validate checks flow to every host or container that runs it.

name.description: Unique name for this script, referenced from a `script:` step by name.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this script does.

language.description: Which interpreter runs the rendered source.

source.description: Path to the script's source file, alongside this definition (e.g. "install-mysql.sh").

timeout.description: Seconds before the step running this script is killed as failed.

args.description: Extra arguments passed to the script when it runs.

ignore_errors.description: If true, a non-zero exit from this script warns instead of failing the whole build.

tags.description: Labels for searching, grouping, and ad-hoc targeting. Flow to every host/container running this script.

findings.description: Findings this script introduces. Travel with the script to every host or container that runs it.
findings.example:
findings:
  - severity: 4
    difficulty: 2
    description: SQL injection in the login form

people.description: People this script concerns, e.g. accounts it creates.

validate.description: Checks run after every host/container's execution of this script, on top of any validate block on the step itself.
